```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(ape)
library(phangorn)
library(seqinr)
library(tidyverse)

dir.create("../output_data", showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("../visuals", showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## Overview

This workflow reconstructs ancestral states of the ATPα (Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase α-subunit)
functional motif across the Danaini phylogeny and tests how sensitive those
reconstructions are. Each taxon's functional state is the three-residue code at
alignment positions **1 / 9 / 12** — VSH, VSN, LSN, QAN or LAN.

The document has three analysis sections plus a methods note:

1. **ATPα ancestral state reconstruction (IQ-TREE)** — maximum-likelihood,
   empirical-Bayes (marginal) reconstruction under the LG amino-acid model on the
   Danaini tree, polarised with the outgroups *Heliconius erato* and
   *Mechanitis polymnia*.
2. **Robustness to phylogenetic uncertainty (bootstrap)** — the reconstruction
   repeated across the 1000 ultrafast-bootstrap trees of the Danaini backbone.
3. **Robustness to taxon sampling (jackknife)** — each sequenced taxon dropped in
   turn to see whether any single taxon drives an ancestral state.
4. **Robustness to incomplete taxon sampling (coverage)** — the reconstruction
   placed on the full Danaini tree, with unsampled taxa entered as missing data,
   to map where ancestral states are well supported versus interpolated across
   sampling gaps.
5. **Note on the AltAll test** — why the standard residue-level robustness check
   (Eick et al. 2017) is uninformative for this particular dataset.

Sections 2–4 use `phangorn` (same LG model) because they refit the model many
times in-process; section 1 confirms `phangorn` and IQ-TREE give the same
ancestral states on the reference tree, so the two are interchangeable here.

## Shared setup: configuration, data and tree

```{r config}
positions <- c(1, 9, 12)                       # ATPα functional sites
AA <- c("A","R","N","D","C","Q","E","G","H","I",
        "L","K","M","F","P","S","T","W","Y","V")
pcol <- paste0("p_", AA)

# Outgroup priority for rooting (reversible model => marginal states are
# root-independent; rooting only fixes orientation and clade definitions).
outgroup_priority <- c("Heliconius_erato", "Mechanitis_polymnia")

state_cols <- c(VSH = "#c43240", VSN = "#f4a261", LSN = "#e9c46a",
                QAN = "#264653", LAN = "#287271")
code_color <- function(code) {
  out <- unname(state_cols[code]); out[is.na(out)] <- "lightgray"; out
}
```

```{r load_data}
sequences <- read.fasta("../input_data/alignment.fasta",
                        seqtype = "AA", as.string = TRUE)
seq_matrix <- matrix(nrow = length(sequences), ncol = nchar(sequences[[1]]))
for (i in seq_along(sequences)) {
  seq_matrix[i, ] <- strsplit(toupper(sequences[[i]]), "")[[1]]
}
rownames(seq_matrix) <- names(sequences)

tree0  <- read.tree("../input_data/Danaini_in_HOSTS.newick")
shared <- intersect(tree0$tip.label, rownames(seq_matrix))
cat("Alignment taxa:", nrow(seq_matrix), "| tree tips:", length(tree0$tip.label),
    "| taxa in both (analysed):", length(shared), "\n")
```

```{r recon_helper}
# Reconstruct ATPα focal states on a tree pruned to `taxa`. Returns the pruned,
# rooted tree and, per internal node, the 3-residue state code and its support
# (minimum of the max-posterior at the three focal positions).
recon <- function(src_tree, taxa) {
  tr <- keep.tip(src_tree, taxa)
  og <- outgroup_priority[outgroup_priority %in% taxa][1]
  if (!is.na(og)) tr <- root(tr, outgroup = og, resolve.root = TRUE)
  tr$node.label <- NULL
  tr <- makeNodeLabel(tr, method = "number", prefix = "N")

  fit <- pml(tr, phyDat(seq_matrix[taxa, , drop = FALSE], type = "AA"),
             model = "LG")
  fit <- optim.pml(fit, model = "LG", optGamma = FALSE, optEdge = TRUE,
                   control = pml.control(trace = 0))
  df <- as.data.frame(anc_pml(fit))
  n_tip <- length(tr$tip.label)

  code <- rep(NA_character_, tr$Nnode)
  supp <- rep(NA_real_, tr$Nnode)
  for (i in seq_len(tr$Nnode)) {
    sub <- df[df$Node == tr$node.label[i], ]
    if (nrow(sub) == 0) next   # phangorn unroots => root node has no state
    best <- vapply(positions, function(st) {
      p <- as.numeric(sub[sub$Site == st, pcol]); c(AA[which.max(p)], max(p))
    }, character(2))
    code[i] <- paste(best[1, ], collapse = "")
    supp[i] <- min(as.numeric(best[2, ]))
  }
  list(tree = tr, n_tip = n_tip, code = code, support = supp)
}

# Internal-node table keyed by descendant-taxon set (stable across prunings).
node_table <- function(rec) {
  map_dfr(seq_len(rec$tree$Nnode), function(i) {
    if (is.na(rec$code[i])) return(NULL)
    tips <- rec$tree$tip.label[Descendants(rec$tree, rec$n_tip + i,
                                           type = "tips")[[1]]]
    if (length(tips) < 2) return(NULL)
    tibble(node_id = rec$n_tip + i, key = paste(sort(tips), collapse = "|"),
           code = rec$code[i], support = rec$support[i])
  })
}
```

---

# 1. ATPα ancestral state reconstruction (IQ-TREE)

The primary reconstruction fixes the Danaini topology (`-te`), re-estimates branch
lengths and model parameters on the ATPα alignment under LG+Γ, and reconstructs
marginal ancestral states (`-asr`), rooted on the outgroups.

## Locate IQ-TREE

```{r iqtree_bin}
iqtree_bin <- Sys.getenv(
  "IQTREE_BIN",
  unset = "/opt/anaconda3/envs/danaini-phylo/bin/iqtree")
if (!file.exists(iqtree_bin)) {
  found <- Sys.which(c("iqtree3", "iqtree2", "iqtree"))
  found <- found[found != ""]
  if (length(found) > 0) iqtree_bin <- unname(found[1]) else
    stop("IQ-TREE not found; set IQTREE_BIN to the binary in your conda env.")
}
cat("IQ-TREE:", iqtree_bin, "\n")
```

## Prune, root and write inputs

```{r iqtree_inputs}
ref_tree <- keep.tip(tree0, shared)
ref_tree <- root(ref_tree, outgroup = "Heliconius_erato", resolve.root = TRUE)

iqtree_dir <- "../output_data/iqtree_asr"
dir.create(iqtree_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
aln_path  <- file.path(iqtree_dir, "atpa_alignment.fasta")
tree_path <- file.path(iqtree_dir, "atpa_fixed_topology.treefile")
prefix    <- file.path(iqtree_dir, "atpa_asr")

seq_list <- lapply(shared, function(t) seq_matrix[t, ])
names(seq_list) <- shared
write.fasta(seq_list, names = shared, file.out = aln_path)
write.tree(ref_tree, file = tree_path)

cat("Analysed taxa:", length(shared), "| alignment sites:", ncol(seq_matrix), "\n")
```

## Run IQ-TREE

```{r iqtree_run}
outgroup_spec <- paste(intersect(outgroup_priority, shared), collapse = ",")
args <- c("-s", aln_path, "-te", tree_path, "-m", "LG+G", "-asr",
          "-o", outgroup_spec, "-pre", prefix, "-nt", "AUTO", "-redo")
log <- system2(iqtree_bin, args, stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE)

state_file <- paste0(prefix, ".state")
if (!file.exists(state_file)) { cat(paste(log, collapse = "\n")); stop("no .state") }
cat("IQ-TREE finished. Model/fit:\n")
cat(paste(grep("Model of substitution|Log-likelihood of the tree",
               readLines(paste0(prefix, ".iqtree")), value = TRUE),
          collapse = "\n"), "\n")
```

## Node posterior probabilities

```{r iqtree_posteriors}
state_raw <- read.table(state_file, header = TRUE, sep = "\t",
                        comment.char = "#", check.names = FALSE)
p_cols <- grep("^p_", names(state_raw), value = TRUE)

posteriors_df <- state_raw %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(p_cols), names_to = "state",
               names_prefix = "p_", values_to = "posterior") %>%
  transmute(site = Site, node_name = Node,
            node = as.integer(factor(Node, levels = unique(Node))),
            state, posterior) %>%
  arrange(site, node, state)

write.csv(posteriors_df, "../output_data/atpalpha_ASR_node_posteriors.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)
cat("Wrote ../output_data/atpalpha_ASR_node_posteriors.csv (",
    nrow(posteriors_df), "rows )\n")
```

## Reconstruction figure

```{r iqtree_figure, fig.width=11, fig.height=9}
iq_tree <- ladderize(read.tree(paste0(prefix, ".treefile")))
n_tip <- length(iq_tree$tip.label)

# Best (max-posterior) state per node/site
node_state <- state_raw %>% transmute(node_name = Node, site = Site, state = State)
anc_mat <- matrix("", nrow = length(unique(node_state$node_name)), ncol = ncol(seq_matrix),
                  dimnames = list(unique(node_state$node_name), NULL))
for (r in seq_len(nrow(node_state)))
  anc_mat[node_state$node_name[r], node_state$site[r]] <- node_state$state[r]

tip_code  <- apply(seq_matrix[iq_tree$tip.label, positions], 1, paste, collapse = "")
node_lab  <- iq_tree$node.label
node_code <- vapply(node_lab, function(nm)
  if (nm %in% rownames(anc_mat)) paste(anc_mat[nm, positions], collapse = "") else NA_character_,
  character(1))

draw_iq <- function() {
  par(mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1))
  plot(iq_tree, cex = 0.75, edge.width = 1.2, label.offset = 0.004,
       main = "ATPA ancestral states (IQ-TREE, LG+G)\nfunctional code at positions 1/9/12")
  tiplabels(pch = 21, bg = code_color(tip_code), col = "black", cex = 1.3, lwd = 0.6)
  for (i in seq_len(iq_tree$Nnode))
    nodelabels(node_code[i], node = n_tip + i, cex = 0.5, frame = "circle",
               bg = code_color(node_code[i]), col = "black")
  legend("bottomleft", bty = "n", title = "ATPA state",
         legend = names(state_cols), pt.bg = state_cols, pch = 21, cex = 0.85)
}
draw_iq()
png("../visuals/atpalpha_ASR_tree.png", width = 1200, height = 1000, res = 120)
draw_iq(); dev.off()
cat("Saved ../visuals/atpalpha_ASR_tree.png\n")
```

## Cross-check: IQ-TREE vs phangorn

Confirms the `phangorn`-LG reconstruction used in the sensitivity sections
reproduces the IQ-TREE states, so the two engines are interchangeable here.

```{r concordance}
ph_ref <- node_table(recon(tree0, shared))
iq_code_by_clade <- function(tips) {
  nid <- getMRCA(iq_tree, tips); nm <- iq_tree$node.label[nid - n_tip]
  if (is.na(nm) || !(nm %in% rownames(anc_mat))) return(NA_character_)
  paste(anc_mat[nm, positions], collapse = "")
}
comp <- ph_ref %>%
  mutate(iqtree = map_chr(strsplit(key, "|", fixed = TRUE), iq_code_by_clade)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(iqtree)) %>%
  mutate(agree = iqtree == code)
cat(sprintf("Shared clades compared: %d | identical state code: %d (%.0f%%)\n",
            nrow(comp), sum(comp$agree), 100 * mean(comp$agree)))
```

# 2. Robustness to phylogenetic uncertainty (bootstrap)

To assess sensitivity to phylogenetic uncertainty, the reconstruction was
repeated across the 1000 ultrafast-bootstrap trees of the Danaini backbone
(Hanson-Smith et al. 2010). In each tree, every ancestral node was located as the
most recent common ancestor of its descendant taxa, allowing homologous nodes to
be compared across differing topologies. For each node we recorded the frequency
with which its defining clade was recovered as monophyletic (topological support)
and the frequency with which its reconstructed state matched the reference
reconstruction (state consistency).

```{r bootstrap}
boot_file <- paste0("../../Extended_Data_Figure1/output_data/danaini_tree/",
                    "supermatrix_ge1/supermatrix_ge1.ufboot")
stopifnot(file.exists(boot_file))

ref <- recon(tree0, shared)
ref_nodes <- node_table(ref) %>%
  mutate(tips = strsplit(key, "|", fixed = TRUE),
         n_taxa = lengths(tips))

boots <- read.tree(boot_file)
n_boot <- length(boots)

n_mono <- integer(nrow(ref_nodes)); n_same <- integer(nrow(ref_nodes))
alt <- vector("list", nrow(ref_nodes))
for (b in seq_len(n_boot)) {
  rb <- recon(boots[[b]], shared); tb <- rb$tree
  for (j in seq_len(nrow(ref_nodes))) {
    S <- ref_nodes$tips[[j]]
    mrca <- getMRCA(tb, S); code <- rb$code[mrca - rb$n_tip]
    if (isTRUE(is.monophyletic(tb, S))) n_mono[j] <- n_mono[j] + 1L
    if (!is.na(code) && code == ref_nodes$code[j]) n_same[j] <- n_same[j] + 1L
    alt[[j]] <- c(alt[[j]], code)
  }
}

boot_df <- ref_nodes %>%
  mutate(clade_freq = n_mono / n_boot,
         state_consistency = n_same / n_boot,
         alt_states = map2_chr(seq_along(alt), code, function(j, rc) {
           tb <- sort(table(alt[[j]]), decreasing = TRUE); tb <- tb[names(tb) != rc]
           if (length(tb) == 0) "" else
             paste(sprintf("%s:%.2f", names(tb), tb / n_boot), collapse = " ")
         })) %>%
  select(node_id, code, n_taxa, clade_freq, state_consistency, alt_states)

write.csv(boot_df, "../output_data/atpalpha_ASR_bootstrap_robustness.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("Bootstrap trees: %d | nodes: %d\n", n_boot, nrow(boot_df)))
cat(sprintf("State matches in >=95%% of trees: %d/%d | median consistency: %.3f\n",
            sum(boot_df$state_consistency >= 0.95), nrow(boot_df),
            median(boot_df$state_consistency)))
```

```{r bootstrap_results}
boot_df %>% arrange(state_consistency) %>%
  select(code, n_taxa, clade_freq, state_consistency, alt_states) %>%
  print(n = 50)
```

```{r bootstrap_scatter, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
plot(boot_df$clade_freq, boot_df$state_consistency, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1),
     pch = 21, bg = code_color(boot_df$code), col = "black", cex = 1.4,
     xlab = "Clade frequency (topological support)",
     ylab = "Ancestral-state consistency",
     main = "A clade can be weakly supported yet have a robust ancestral state")
abline(0, 1, lty = 3, col = "grey60"); abline(h = 0.95, lty = 3, col = "grey50")
```

```{r bootstrap_figure, fig.width=11, fig.height=9}
tp <- ladderize(ref$tree); nt <- ref$n_tip
tip_code <- apply(seq_matrix[tp$tip.label, positions], 1, paste, collapse = "")
idx <- match((nt + 1):(nt + tp$Nnode), boot_df$node_id)
nd_fill <- code_color(boot_df$code[idx]); nd_fill[is.na(idx)] <- "grey85"
cons <- ifelse(is.na(idx), NA, boot_df$state_consistency[idx])
nd_out <- ifelse(!is.na(cons) & cons < 0.95, "red", "black")
nd_lwd <- ifelse(!is.na(cons) & cons < 0.95, 2.4, 0.6)
nd_cex <- 0.5 + 2.3 * ifelse(is.na(cons), 0, cons)

draw_boot <- function() {
  par(mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1))
  plot(tp, cex = 0.75, edge.width = 1.2, label.offset = 0.004,
       main = "ATPA states across 1000 bootstrap trees\n(node size = state consistency; red outline = < 95%)")
  tiplabels(pch = 21, bg = code_color(tip_code), col = "black", cex = 1.3, lwd = 0.6)
  nodelabels(pch = 21, bg = nd_fill, col = nd_out, cex = nd_cex, lwd = nd_lwd)
  legend("bottomleft", bty = "n", title = "ATPA state",
         legend = names(state_cols), pt.bg = state_cols, pch = 21, cex = 0.85)
}
draw_boot()
png("../visuals/atpalpha_ASR_bootstrap.png", width = 1200, height = 1000, res = 120)
draw_boot(); dev.off()
cat("Saved ../visuals/atpalpha_ASR_bootstrap.png\n")
```

---

# 3. Robustness to taxon sampling (jackknife)

Each of the `r length(shared)` sequenced taxa is dropped in turn and the
reconstruction repeated on the remaining taxa. For every reference node we record
whether its state is unchanged; a flip names the taxon the state depended on.

```{r jackknife}
base_tbl <- node_table(recon(tree0, shared))

stab <- base_tbl %>%
  mutate(n_rep = 0L, n_stable = 0L, min_support_rep = support,
         alt_states = "", driver = NA_character_)

for (t in shared) {
  rep_tbl <- node_table(recon(tree0, setdiff(shared, t)))
  look <- setNames(seq_len(nrow(rep_tbl)), rep_tbl$key)
  for (j in seq_len(nrow(stab))) {
    k2 <- paste(setdiff(strsplit(stab$key[j], "|", fixed = TRUE)[[1]], t),
                collapse = "|")
    if (!is.na(look[k2])) {
      r <- rep_tbl[look[k2], ]
      stab$n_rep[j] <- stab$n_rep[j] + 1L
      stab$min_support_rep[j] <- min(stab$min_support_rep[j], r$support)
      if (r$code == stab$code[j]) stab$n_stable[j] <- stab$n_stable[j] + 1L
      else {
        stab$alt_states[j] <- paste(unique(c(
          if (nzchar(stab$alt_states[j])) stab$alt_states[j], r$code)), collapse = ",")
        stab$driver[j] <- paste(na.omit(unique(c(stab$driver[j], t))), collapse = ";")
      }
    }
  }
}
stab <- stab %>%
  mutate(stability = ifelse(n_rep > 0, n_stable / n_rep, NA_real_),
         n_taxa = lengths(strsplit(key, "|", fixed = TRUE))) %>%
  arrange(stability)

write.csv(stab %>% select(code, n_taxa, n_rep, n_stable, stability,
                          support, min_support_rep, alt_states, driver),
          "../output_data/atpalpha_ASR_jackknife_stability.csv", row.names = FALSE)

n_comp <- sum(stab$n_rep); n_flip <- sum(stab$n_rep - stab$n_stable)
cat(sprintf("Node x replicate comparisons: %d | state changes: %d (%.2f%%)\n",
            n_comp, n_flip, 100 * n_flip / n_comp))
cat(sprintf("Nodes never flipped: %d of %d\n",
            sum(stab$stability == 1), nrow(stab)))

cat("\nNodes that ever change state when a taxon is dropped:\n")
stab %>% filter(stability < 1) %>%
  select(code, n_taxa, stability, alt_states, driver) %>% print(n = 50)
```

```{r jackknife_figure, fig.width=11, fig.height=9}
tj <- ladderize(recon(tree0, shared)$tree); nt <- length(tj$tip.label)
tip_code <- apply(seq_matrix[tj$tip.label, positions], 1, paste, collapse = "")
idx <- match((nt + 1):(nt + tj$Nnode), stab$node_id)
nd_fill <- code_color(stab$code[idx]); nd_fill[is.na(idx)] <- "grey85"
nd_out  <- ifelse(!is.na(idx) & stab$stability[idx] < 1, "red", "black")
nd_lwd  <- ifelse(!is.na(idx) & stab$stability[idx] < 1, 2.4, 0.6)
nd_cex  <- 0.6 + 2.2 * ifelse(is.na(idx), 0, stab$min_support_rep[idx])

draw_jk <- function() {
  par(mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1))
  plot(tj, cex = 0.75, edge.width = 1.2, label.offset = 0.004,
       main = "Leave-one-taxon-out jackknife of ATPA states\n(red outline = state flips when some taxon dropped)")
  tiplabels(pch = 21, bg = code_color(tip_code), col = "black", cex = 1.3, lwd = 0.6)
  nodelabels(pch = 21, bg = nd_fill, col = nd_out, cex = nd_cex, lwd = nd_lwd)
  legend("bottomleft", bty = "n", title = "ATPA state",
         legend = names(state_cols), pt.bg = state_cols, pch = 21, cex = 0.85)
}
draw_jk()
png("../visuals/atpalpha_ASR_jackknife.png", width = 1200, height = 1000, res = 120)
draw_jk(); dev.off()
cat("Saved ../visuals/atpalpha_ASR_jackknife.png\n")
```

---

# 4. Robustness to incomplete taxon sampling (coverage)

Only `r length(shared)` of the Danaini tree's tips carry ATPα data; the main
reconstruction prunes the rest away. Here we instead place the reconstruction on
the **full tree**, entering the unsampled taxa as missing data, to show where
ancestral states are genuinely supported versus interpolated across sampling
gaps. IQ-TREE rejects all-gap sequences, so this uses `phangorn` (LG), which
tolerates them; we confirm it reproduces the Section 1 states where they overlap.

```{r coverage_build}
ftree <- root(tree0, outgroup = "Heliconius_erato", resolve.root = TRUE)
ftree$node.label <- NULL
ftree <- ladderize(makeNodeLabel(ftree, method = "number", prefix = "Node"))
n_ftip <- length(ftree$tip.label)
n_site <- ncol(seq_matrix)

data_taxa    <- intersect(ftree$tip.label, rownames(seq_matrix))
missing_taxa <- setdiff(ftree$tip.label, rownames(seq_matrix))
cat(sprintf("Full tree: %d tips | with ATPA data: %d | missing (gaps): %d (%.0f%%)\n",
            n_ftip, length(data_taxa), length(missing_taxa),
            100 * length(missing_taxa) / n_ftip))

full_rows <- lapply(ftree$tip.label, function(t)
  if (t %in% rownames(seq_matrix)) seq_matrix[t, ] else rep("-", n_site))
names(full_rows) <- ftree$tip.label
full_mat <- do.call(rbind, full_rows)
```

```{r coverage_reconstruct}
cfit <- pml(ftree, phyDat(full_mat, type = "AA"), model = "LG")
cfit <- optim.pml(cfit, model = "LG", optGamma = FALSE, optEdge = TRUE,
                  control = pml.control(trace = 0))
anc_df <- as.data.frame(anc_pml(cfit))
fp_cols <- grep("^p_", names(anc_df), value = TRUE)

posteriors_full <- anc_df %>% filter(Node %in% ftree$node.label) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(fp_cols), names_to = "state",
               names_prefix = "p_", values_to = "posterior") %>%
  transmute(site = Site, node_name = Node, state, posterior) %>%
  arrange(site, node_name, state)
write.csv(posteriors_full,
          "../output_data/atpalpha_ASR_full_tree_posteriors.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("Wrote ../output_data/atpalpha_ASR_full_tree_posteriors.csv\n")
```

```{r coverage_table}
best_at <- function(nl, site) {
  row <- anc_df[anc_df$Node == nl & anc_df$Site == site, fp_cols]
  j <- which.max(as.numeric(row))
  c(state = sub("^p_", "", fp_cols[j]), p = as.numeric(row)[j])
}
# phangorn unroots => the root node has no reconstruction; drive off present labels
rec_nodes <- intersect(ftree$node.label, unique(anc_df$Node))
coverage_df <- map_dfr(rec_nodes, function(lab) {
  nid  <- n_ftip + match(lab, ftree$node.label)
  tips <- ftree$tip.label[Descendants(ftree, nid, type = "tips")[[1]]]
  calls <- vapply(positions, function(s) best_at(lab, s), character(2))
  tibble(node = lab, n_descendants = length(tips),
         n_with_data = sum(tips %in% data_taxa),
         coverage = sum(tips %in% data_taxa) / length(tips),
         state_code = paste(calls["state", ], collapse = ""),
         support = min(as.numeric(calls["p", ]))) }) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_descendants))
write.csv(coverage_df, "../output_data/atpalpha_ASR_coverage.csv", row.names = FALSE)

cat(sprintf("Internal nodes: %d | zero-data (pure interpolation): %d | support >= 0.9: %d\n",
            nrow(coverage_df), sum(coverage_df$n_with_data == 0),
            sum(coverage_df$support >= 0.9)))
```

```{r coverage_concordance}
# Cross-check: full-tree states vs the Section 1 IQ-TREE states on shared clades
full_code <- function(tips) {
  nid <- getMRCA(ftree, tips)
  coverage_df$state_code[match(ftree$node.label[nid - n_ftip], coverage_df$node)]
}
iq_code3 <- function(nm) if (!is.na(nm) && nm %in% rownames(anc_mat))
  paste(anc_mat[nm, positions], collapse = "") else NA_character_
niq <- length(iq_tree$tip.label)
ccomp <- map_dfr(seq_len(iq_tree$Nnode), function(i) {
  tips <- iq_tree$tip.label[Descendants(iq_tree, niq + i, type = "tips")[[1]]]
  if (length(tips) < 2) return(NULL)
  tibble(iqtree = iq_code3(iq_tree$node.label[i]), full_tree = full_code(tips))
}) %>% filter(!is.na(iqtree) & !is.na(full_tree)) %>% mutate(agree = iqtree == full_tree)
cat(sprintf("Full-tree vs IQ-TREE on shared clades: %d/%d identical (%.0f%%)\n",
            sum(ccomp$agree), nrow(ccomp), 100 * mean(ccomp$agree)))
```

```{r coverage_scatter, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
rho <- cor(coverage_df$coverage, coverage_df$support, method = "spearman")
plot(coverage_df$coverage, coverage_df$support, pch = 21,
     bg = code_color(coverage_df$state_code), col = "black", cex = 1.3,
     xlab = "Descendant taxon coverage (fraction with data)",
     ylab = "Node support (min posterior at 1/9/12)",
     main = sprintf("Support vs coverage across %d nodes (Spearman rho = %.2f)",
                    nrow(coverage_df), rho))
abline(h = 0.9, lty = 3, col = "grey50")
```

```{r coverage_figure, fig.width=12, fig.height=16}
substituted <- c("Danaus_eresimus", "Danaus_melanippus", "Euploea_core", "Heliconius_erato")
tip_code <- apply(full_mat[ftree$tip.label, positions], 1, paste, collapse = "")
tip_has  <- ftree$tip.label %in% data_taxa
tip_bg   <- ifelse(tip_has, code_color(tip_code), "white")
tip_pch  <- ifelse(!tip_has, 1, ifelse(ftree$tip.label %in% substituted, 22, 21))

ord <- match(ftree$node.label, coverage_df$node)
nd_col <- code_color(coverage_df$state_code[ord]); nd_col[is.na(ord)] <- "grey80"
nd_cex <- 0.5 + 2.2 * coverage_df$support[ord];    nd_cex[is.na(ord)] <- 0.3

draw_cov <- function() {
  par(mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1))
  plot(ftree, cex = 0.55, edge.width = 1, label.offset = 0.01,
       main = "Full-tree ancestral ATPA states with taxon coverage\n(node size = posterior support)")
  tiplabels(pch = tip_pch, bg = tip_bg, col = "black", cex = 0.9, lwd = 0.6)
  nodelabels(pch = 21, bg = nd_col, col = "black", cex = nd_cex, lwd = 0.5)
  legend("bottomleft", bty = "n", title = "ATPA state",
         legend = names(state_cols), pt.bg = state_cols, pch = 21, cex = 0.8)
  legend("left", bty = "n", title = "tip data",
         legend = c("sequenced", "substituted", "no data"),
         pch = c(21, 22, 1), pt.bg = c("grey40", "grey40", "white"), cex = 0.8)
}
draw_cov()
png("../visuals/atpalpha_ASR_coverage.png", width = 1200, height = 1600, res = 120)
draw_cov(); dev.off()
cat("Saved ../visuals/atpalpha_ASR_coverage.png\n")
```

**Interpretation.** Only ~1/3 of the tree is sampled, yet the reconstruction is
robust where it matters: the full-tree analysis reproduces the Section 1 states
on every shared clade, well-covered nodes are confidently reconstructed, and the
low-support nodes are exactly those sitting inside unsampled regions (the
support–coverage correlation). The gaps are visible and flagged, but they do not
bias the sampled reconstruction.

---

# 5. Note: why the AltAll residue-level test is uninformative here

A third gold-standard ASR robustness check is **AltAll** (Eick, Bridgham,
Anderson, Harms & Thornton 2017): build an alternative ancestor that substitutes
the *second-most-probable* residue at every ambiguously reconstructed position,
and confirm the conclusion holds for both the maximum-a-posteriori and the AltAll
sequence. We ran it and it is **trivially satisfied here** — not because the
analysis is weak, but because of the structure of this dataset. 

```{r altall_evidence}
# (a) Only the functional columns vary at all
var_cols <- which(apply(seq_matrix[shared, ], 2,
                        function(c) length(unique(c)) > 1))
cat("Variable alignment columns:", paste(var_cols, collapse = ", "),
    "(all other sites invariant)\n")

# (b) At the focal positions, the second-best residue is essentially zero
foc <- state_raw[state_raw$Site %in% positions, ]
p2 <- apply(foc[, p_cols], 1, function(p) sort(p, decreasing = TRUE)[2])
cat(sprintf("Max 2nd-best posterior at any focal node/position: %.4f\n", max(p2)))
cat("AltAll cutoff is typically 0.20 -> no residue qualifies for swapping.\n")
```

**Interpretation.** The 12-residue ATPα motif varies at only the three focal
positions, so the ancestral sequence reduces to the state code and AltAll over
the sequence is AltAll over positions 1/9/12. Because this short alignment
carries so little variation, branch lengths estimated from it collapse toward
zero, leaving effectively no evolutionary distance along which an internal node
could differ from its neighbours. Every focal position is therefore reconstructed
deterministically (second-best posterior ≈ 0, far below the 0.20 threshold) under
both IQ-TREE and phangorn-LG, and the MAP and AltAll sequences are identical.
AltAll is thus uninformative here by construction, not because the reconstruction
is weak; the informative axes of uncertainty for this dataset are phylogenetic
(Section 2) and taxon sampling (Section 3).
